title: Describe drainage, grade and base
intro: A pavement is a layered structure that must carry loads and manage water. A smooth new surface will not correct an unstable foundation or a blocked drainage route. Reading the whole road helps the crew protect access to homes, services and community spaces.

sections.title: Describe proper road drainage
sections.text: Surface water follows crossfall, longitudinal grade and low points toward an approved collection route. Subsurface water needs its own drainage path. Inspect ditches, catch basins, culverts and outlets against the drawings; a visible inlet is not proof of a functioning outlet. Sediment, fuel and uncured materials must be kept out of drainage systems. Do not redirect water toward neighbouring land or a watercourse because that route looks convenient. Report ponding, erosion and blocked drainage before covering the evidence. Approved environmental controls and local access commitments belong in the work plan.

sections.title: Describe sub grade
sections.text: Subgrade is the prepared soil foundation beneath the pavement structure. Soil type, moisture, density, frost susceptibility and soft areas influence performance. Rutting under equipment, pumping water and inconsistent support require evaluation; adding asphalt is not a substitute for correcting the cause. Geotextiles can separate materials or provide filtration, depending on the specified product and design. Geogrids have different functions. Check product identity, overlap, orientation and protection requirements before placement. Damaged or wrongly installed fabric cannot be assumed effective because it is hidden.

sections.title: Describe sub-base
sections.text: Sub-base distributes loading and can provide a working platform or drainage function. Its specified grading, thickness, moisture and compaction requirements govern placement. Approved recycled material may be suitable, but availability alone does not establish compliance. Place in controlled lifts, protect against contamination and check each accepted layer before burying it. Segregation, excessive fines and trapped water can change how the layer behaves. Record the material source and test results so a later concern can be traced to an actual location and lift.

sections.title: Describe base
sections.text: Base is the prepared layer directly supporting the asphalt in a typical flexible pavement. Crushed aggregate from a quarry or pit, approved dredged or river-derived material, and recycled products each require the project’s source authorization and material acceptance. Their names do not establish equal performance or permission to extract them. Check surface elevation, crossfall, density, cleanliness and drainage. A thin low spot in the base changes asphalt demand and may create a local thickness problem. Maintain the accepted base until paving starts; traffic or rain can alter it after inspection.

worked.title: Follow the water
worked.case: A 120 m access road has a sound-looking base. A blocked catch basin sits at its low point, and water is pumping through one wheel path. The paving crew is ready.
worked.solution: Hold the affected work and identify the drainage and support problems. Protect public access and the inlet, document the location, and request the responsible person’s correction and acceptance. Do not treat extra asphalt as a drainage repair. Record the repaired outlet and accepted foundation before release.

activities.prompt: Draw the four typical layers from prepared soil to asphalt. Label one check at each interface.
activities.answer: From bottom: subgrade—support/moisture; sub-base—approved material and accepted lift; base—grade/crossfall/cleanliness; asphalt—specified mixture and compacted thickness. Actual designs may omit or add layers; use the project section.

activities.prompt: An approved 80 m × 4 m sub-base lift is 0.15 m compacted thickness. Find its compacted volume. Can you order that many loose cubic metres without further information?
activities.answer: 80 × 4 × 0.15 = 48 m³ compacted. Loose supply volume requires a justified conversion or project allowance; 48 m³ loose is not automatically enough.
activities.title: An approved 80 m × 4 m sub-base lift is 0.15 m compacted thickness

activities.prompt: A partner proposes opening a ditch toward a nearby creek to remove ponded water. Give a respectful response and a next step.
activities.answer: Explain that drainage changes need the approved design and environmental controls. Hold the change, notify the responsible person and obtain an authorized solution that protects the watercourse and neighbouring land.

Record and communicate a foundation defect before covering it.
